### Readings for Next Week (and Quiz 4)

1.  [**Read my brief overview on Measures**](/rm/readings/Measures.qmd)**.** Focus on the different strengths and limitations of self-reports and observational methods. We will focus on observational methods next week, but it might be helpful to have some background on self-report methods to help differentiate the strengths & limitations.

2.  [**Read this chapter on Observational Research**](https://kpu.pressbooks.pub/psychmethods4e/chapter/observational-research/)**.** You can skim much of this, but focus on the different types of observational studies.

3.  [**Read through the chapter on the Specific Affect Coding System (SPAFF)**](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/4ggh81t64qnvz5kjrqukn/4_SPAFF_CodingScheme_ShortExcerpt.pdf?rlkey=e9er6moatfgk96du9zz3khazs&e=1&dl=0)**.** This is an example of a guide for researchers interested in making observations of emotion. Focus on the "three rules" of people watching, and the different guidelines for behavioral coding (e.g., function, indicator, cues, counter-indicators). You can skim the stuff on "Action Units" in the face, though note this is an example of how psychologists have tried to quantify emotion with numbers like "REAL SCIENTISTS".

### Week 4 Discussion Questions.

**YOUR POST :** Submit answers to the [Vision Board](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14u3w5edvo6KSFRw2U9t1knDANFSGBWOvDjS7-ZGujos/edit?usp=sharing) so we can more easily see this work together in class. You do not need to submit anything to the Canvas assignment; I'll use this to keep track of grading. Thanks!

1.  **From the Chapter on Measures.** Answer the final question in the reading (*`"If you look like you are smiling and have the neurotransmitter levels that suggest you are happy and our $600/hour test says that your brain is activated in a way consistent with happiness, but you FEEL and SAY you are miserable....are you happy?"`*) Why did you choose this answer?

2.  **From the SPAFF Reading.** Try using the "three rules" of people watching to observe someone. Describe who you chose to observe. Then, describe a specific way that each of the three rules informed your observations of the person (what insights did you learn or gain)? I've posted an example of this in the Vision Board (and the required reply below.)

3.  **We Love Bread (REPLY TO ANOTHER STUDENT).** Look over another student's post on the Vision Board for Question 2. What is one variable that you would label for their observation? Then, think about how this variable might be measured with a self-report. Give an example of how this variable might be high or low in either a) self-insight OR b) self-diminishment/enhancement.
